shared_direction: Wide landscape 3:2 editorial technical plate, part of a coherent series about generative wooden jigsaws. Warm white untextured sheet, near-black ink, cobalt blue for construction geometry, a single signal vermilion for key marks. Beautiful scientific line engraving and exceptionally clear geometry. Flat, disciplined technical manual design with a large left-aligned neo-grotesque heading, short direct labels, a generous outer margin. Strong scale hierarchy. No UI panels, numbering, logo, page furniture, filler, gradients, or ornamental arrows. This is a scientific explanatory illustration, not a precise cut file. All displayed text should be spelled exactly as provided, in English.

figures.prompt: Create "From image to interlock". Redraw the supplied physical puzzle reference into a NEW original explanatory figure, changing everything except the general real birch material and the principle of figural pieces. The specific educational story: one broad, simply lobed oak leaf serves as the OUTER board outline, with a tiny fixed beetle-shaped whimsy inside. Lay out a generous 2x2 sequence of four clearly separated, large specimens read across then down, with arrows only if they help. First upper left: a naturalistic overhead photo of ONE oak leaf next to a small flat black binary mask of exactly its outline. Label "Extract the outline". Upper right: the same outer leaf perimeter, occupied by a sparse irregular Voronoi tessellation in thin cobalt with a few red seed points, a single black beetle silhouette fixed inside one region near center; label "Place seeds and a whimsy". Lower left: an overhead blueprint of exactly the same leaf, tiny beetle preserved, cells turned into organic mutual interlocking pieces; one continuous shared seam emphasized in red. Label "Grow shared seams". Lower right: a broad and beautiful physical rendering of that SAME oak-leaf-shaped puzzle in honey birch plywood with fine, dark, organic through-cuts. One beetle-shaped piece slightly lifted above its matching recess; clearly has some thickness. Label "Cut once in wood". This is the customer-art + fixed figure + generated common boundary concept from a studio's published process. Avoid conventional grid jigsaw tabs, a pile of leaves, or showing a different exterior at each step.

Create "Six ways to shape a seam". Comparative morphology chart of six published Nervous System cut styles. A tidy 3 columns × 2 rows field guide, each specimen labeled once, with one large 2D connected seam separating a soft graphite-light region from white. The edge must be continuous, like matching faces of two jigsaw pieces. Show dark lines, cobalt detail showing underlying construction only, restrained red mark for a growth cue. No characters or other imagery. Top left "Dendrite" then smaller "Branching growth": interlocking rounded antler branches that fork. Top middle "Amoeba" then "Fine branching": comb-like smaller repetitive, high-frequency blunt cilia nesting within narrow opposing bays. Top right "Maze" then "Elastic rods": single packed serpentine seam forming long narrow winding fingers with tight hairpin bends, resembling an elongated glyph; no literal labyrinth walls. Bottom left "Wave" then "Vortices": single continuous beautiful sweeping fluid seam curling into a spiral with the reverse curve curling out and away, no dead-end or detached swirl. Bottom middle "Coral" then "Circular arcs": chained, variable-radius circular arcs forming looping rounded lobes; two faint construction circles make the mechanism visible. Bottom right "Matrix" then "Cell exchanges": stepped, sharply angular hooked staircase between pieces on a lightly warped quadrilateral mesh, with one red cell transferred across. Typographic labels beneath each specimen. No repeated patterns across specimens, no shadow or material rendering, no hard card frames, no axes or numbers. Show a genuinely different geometric operation in each.

Use the reference image as the technical source for the ACTUAL angular forked motif, the fixed red base contour and examples of its dark deformed outlines. Redesign that material as an editorial figure titled "Learning a piece". This is PathNet v2. Left, an oversized charcoal silhouette faithfully based on one recognizable unchanged angular, forked hook in the upper row of the reference, traced exactly around its perimeter with a thin vermilion line. Mid-ground, four carefully drawn overlapped comparisons in a 2×2 specimen array: each one shows a dark contour changing slightly in shoulder, inner fork or tip against the IDENTICAL fixed thin red base outline. At right, a single very large closeup of its fork open to the outside: a distinct round-neck junction, one thin cobalt double-headed dimension THROUGH the narrow bridge of solid material and a separate dimension through the WHITE gap BETWEEN two arms. Keep dimension marks visibly separate and readable. Rather than put numbers on inaccurate drawings, label the two concepts only: "Neck width" and "Clearance". Under the left and middle specimens, simple labels "Base outline" and "Shape variants". Along the lower margin use the single accurate line "Reference piece at 34 mm: neck 2.92 mm, clearance 2.91 mm." Numbers belong to the base glyph only. No axes, grid of dozens, copied screenshots, mechanical drawings, camouflage shapes, disconnected triangles or invented measurements. The dark vs red comparison should be discernible at a glance.
